title: Cascade Optimizer Playground: guided sandbox for cache & batch tuning
creator: Ethan Morales
description:
Problem: Customers struggle to pick caching and batching configurations that reduce cost without regressing latency or model quality. Existing interfaces surface raw knobs (batch size, prefill ttl, kv-cache scope) but lack a compact, scenario-driven playground that lets engineers preview trade-offs, run lightweight sims, and apply safe presets with audit trails.

Goal: Design an interactive 'Cascade Optimizer' playground inside Redwood Console that guides users through three core flows: 1) Quick Preset (one-click cost/latency wins), 2) Scenario Tuner (simulate 3 traffic profiles against sample prompts), 3) Guardrail Composer (create safe fallback policies and approval annotations). The UI should be compact (fits inside an Ops panel), surface per-route cost delta estimates, and provide explainers for why the recommendation was chosen.

Approach: Create a horizontally split panel: left side - Scenario Builder (traffic profile selector, sample prompt set picker, sequence length distribution slider); right side - Recommendation Stack (ranked presets with estimated cost savings, delta latency, and risk score). A bottom timeline visualizes token throughput, hit-rate improvement from caching, and a confidence band for predicted latency. Add inline microcopy explaining KV cache scope vs prefill heuristics and a one-click preview that opens a sandbox to run 50 synthetic requests.

Research & constraints: We held 3 shadow sessions with platform engineers and 2 customer interviews (mid-market search SaaS and enterprise assistant). Key constraints: (1) backend sim API returns noisy estimates — UI must show confidence bands and avoid absolutes; (2) some customers require audit trails so every applied preset must attach a reason and optional ticket link; (3) guardrail rules must be expressible as simple predicates (e.g., max_p99_latency <= 200ms OR cost_delta >= -10%).

Design tradeoffs considered: inline vs modal preview (chose inline to reduce context switching), prescriptive labels vs raw controls (provide both — 'Recommended preset' and 'Advanced toggle'). We intentionally prioritize clarity over exposing every internal flag — advanced users can expand an 'Expert' drawer to tune kernel-level hints.

Outcomes expected: Faster time-to-safety for ops teams, measurable per-route cost reduction (target 12% median), and reduced support escalation for misconfigured batch/cache policies.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype linked and annotated with flows for Quick Preset, Scenario Tuner, Guardrail Composer
Prototype includes sample prompts and three traffic profiles (burst, steady, conversational) for sim runs
Recommendation Stack shows estimated cost delta, p50/p95 latency delta, and risk score with confidence band
One-click apply attaches user note and optional ticket ID, recorded in audit log stub
Design tokens and spacing conform to Console design system; interactions documented for ENG handoff
Security review notes captured and any PII in sample prompts redacted
